title: tenant-data-classifier-and-audit-redaction-pipeline
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Customers have asked for stronger assurance that high-sensitivity tenant data is (1) tracked at ingestion, (2) encrypted with region-appropriate CMKs, and (3) produced in audit trails with graded fidelity so that PII does not leak into long-lived logs. This PR implements a tenant-level Data Classification Enforcer and an Audit Redaction Router that work together with RBAC v2 and the KMS affinity layer.

Goals implemented in this PR: 1) Classification service: a lightweight per-request classifier that tags payloads with a sensitivity level (public, internal, confidential, restricted). Tags are attached as immutable attributes on the request context and surfaced to downstream middleware. 2) KMS affinity: classification-driven CMK selection so that restricted/confidential payloads are routed to region-bound CMKs when available; falls back to the tenant's default CMK with a telemetry spike when affinity isn't available. 3) RBAC integration: new RBAC v2 policy predicates that require the 'data:sensitivity:read' scope for reading high-sensitivity artifacts; operator roles without that scope are denied at the policy-evaluator gate. 4) Audit redaction router: audit events are routed to two sinks depending on classification and policy: a low-fidelity public audit (PII-stripped) and a high-fidelity secure audit stored in the encrypted audit-archive service (access requires audit:forensics permission). 5) Migration hooks and feature gate: a migration that backfills classification tags for in-flight jobs where possible, and a rollout feature flag audit_segmentation that enables the router per-tenant. 6) Observability and SLO impacts: added metrics and a small benchmark confirming <2% p95 latency increase on the request path for the classifier in production-like workloads.

Description of changes (single-line summary): Adds classification service, classification-to-kms mapping, RBAC predicates for sensitivity-aware access, audit redaction router and storage integration, tests and migration hooks, telemetry and docs.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for classifier logic and RBAC predicate mapping - [x] Integration tests for KMS affinity routing (mocked CMKs) - [x] E2E tests for audit routing under feature gate - [x] Load tests showing latency regression within acceptable bounds - [x] Migration script and rollback plan - [x] Docs/console UX notes for admins

Commits (high level): - feat(classifier): add tenant data classification microservice and API client - feat(kms): mapping layer to select CMK by classification + region affinity - feat(rbacv2): new predicate "sensitivity_level" and scope checks - feat(audit): audit redaction router + secure-archive sink integration - chore(migrations): backfill classifications for recent jobs - test: integration and e2e tests for classification and audit routing - docs: admin guides and console copy for enabling audit_segmentation

Files changed (high level): - services/classifier/*: new service implementation, client, and tests - services/kms-mapper/*: mapping logic and affinity policy - services/rbacv2/policies/*: new predicate and policy examples - services/audit/router/*: router implementation and secure-archive sink - migrations/2026_02_backfill_classification.sql: DB backfill task - docs/security/audit-classification.md: admin guidance and migration notes - telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics definitions - e2e/tests/audit_segmentation.test.ts: e2e coverage for routing

Review thread summary: - Luca Moretti (reviewer): requested tightening of predicate semantics and an explicit deny-by-default unit test for the RBAC evaluator. Comments: "Predicate mapping is good; add a unit test where an operator without data:sensitivity:read tries to access a restricted artifact and is explicitly denied by the evaluator (not a downstream error)." Response: added rbacv2/evaluator/deny_default.test.go and updated evaluator to short-circuit with explicit deny when predicate missing. - Priya Shah: asked for clearer telemetry for KMS fallback cases and a new metric kms.affinity.fallback_rate. Response: added metric and dashboard tile, and implemented tagging in the mapper to emit fallback_reason and tenant_id. - Marcus Lee: safety checks in migration: "ensure backfill is idempotent and does not reclassify already-tagged items." Response: migration updated to skip rows where classification IS NOT NULL; documented rollback steps.

CI and checks: - build: pass - unit: pass - integration: pass (mock KMS) - e2e: pass - lint: pass - security-scan: one low-severity finding in a helper, fixed in commit 3 - perf-canary: p95 latency +1.6% on a 500rps benchmark (acceptable under SLO).

Performance summary: synthetic throughput test (500 rps, mixed request sizes) shows median latency +0.5%, p95 +1.6% primarily due to classification lookup; KMS selection path negligible when cache warm. Classification CPU cost measured at ~0.8ms per request on a c6i-equivalent host; we added a per-tenant cache with 5m TTL to reduce repeated model lookups.

Security notes: - Classification decisions are only stored as attributes and not used to mutate payloads. - The secure audit sink writes with tenant-scoped CMKs and enforces HSM-backed keys where available. - Access to high-fidelity audit requires audit:forensics scope in RBAC v2 and an additional 'audit_access' claim check in the service token.

Migration and rollout plan: 1) Deploy behind feature flag audit_segmentation=off for one week while running migrations in dry-run mode. 2) Run backfill migration with a small subset of active tenants and validate. 3) Gradual enable per-tenant via console for 5% -> 25% -> 100% rollout with health checks. 4) Monitor kms.affinity.fallback_rate and audit.router.drop_rate for anomalies.

Related work items: Linear ENG-4021 (classification infra), ENG-3999 (kmp/kms affinity), SEC-114 (audit retention policy) and support tickets SUP-889 and INT-2101.

Merge notes: squash-merged after addressing reviewer feedback and fixing a small race in the migration script.

release_notes: Adds tenant data classification and audit redaction routing. Enables region-aware CMK selection based on classification. Introduces RBAC predicates for sensitivity-aware access and a feature-flagged rollout. This is opt-in until officially enabled per-tenant. See docs/security/audit-classification.md for admin steps.
notes_for_ops: When enabling audit_segmentation, watch metrics: kms.affinity.fallback_rate, audit.router.drop_rate and audit.router.secure_sink_success. If fallback_rate > 1% for an extended period, investigate CMK provisioning or update tenant CMK mappings.
